name: Adam Bandt
description: Australian parliamentarian assessed through his civil-rights, public investment and environmental policy programme.

axes.brief: He seeks change through competitive parliamentary elections, referendums and grassroots mobilisation, opposing erosion of basic rights by emergency executive power.
axes.counterEvidence: His acceptance of parliamentary leadership and negotiated legislation qualifies treating every decision as a direct public vote.

axes.brief: His legal work and political programme emphasise civil rights, cannabis legalisation, protest and opposition to arbitrary detention.
axes.counterEvidence: Public-health protection and restrictions on racial hatred coexist with civil liberties; neither unlimited weapons access nor total freedom from safety regulation follows.

axes.brief: He supports Indigenous Treaty, Truth and Voice and a plural Australian community with protection from racism.
axes.counterEvidence: Shared civic participation remains compatible with distinct cultures; removing the flag from a press conference does not settle all integration duties.

axes.brief: He opposes mandatory asylum detention and backs humanitarian protection and cultural inclusion.
axes.counterEvidence: Ending mandatory detention does not itself repeal every visa or border rule; broad numerical-cap and university-route answers remain qualified contextual inferences.

axes.brief: He rejects AUKUS expenditure and prioritises diplomacy and climate security over military escalation.
axes.counterEvidence: Criticism of submarines is not a refusal to defend Australia against attack; defensive preparedness qualifies absolute opposition to military spending.

axes.brief: He invokes international climate science, human rights and UN scrutiny while defending an independent Australian republic.
axes.counterEvidence: Republican sovereignty does not entail rejection of international obligations; ending AUKUS qualifies unconditional long-term military commitments.

qualifications.13: Humanitarian responsibility and administrative control of entry coexist; no exclusive allocation of all border authority is documented.
qualifications.15: International cooperation is explicit, but joining a political federation is a stronger institutional step.

axes.brief: He explicitly favours public housing, public wealth and government enterprise while leaving space for ordinary private businesses.
axes.counterEvidence: Taxing private firms and abolishing fossil subsidies are not the same as nationalising every firm or resource operation.

axes.brief: His programme prioritises workers, environmental standards and domestic transition investment while retaining international economic cooperation.
axes.counterEvidence: Direct tariff evidence is weaker than climate and labour evidence; industrial investment should not be equated automatically with import prohibitions.

qualifications.6: Trade openness and enforceable social and environmental standards make unconditional unilateral liberalisation a mixed proposition.
qualifications.11: Defensive retaliation and the cost to consumers supply competing considerations.

axes.brief: He proposes a Green New Deal, rent freezes, public investment and stronger wage protection within a continuing mixed economy.
axes.counterEvidence: Strong public planning and selective price controls do not establish ordinary compulsory targets for every private industry.

qualifications.16: Coordinated transition investment and ordinary decentralised production coexist; a blanket national production plan exceeds the documented programme.

axes.brief: He favours lifting income support above poverty, taxing large corporate gains and redirecting high-income tax concessions toward households needing support.
axes.counterEvidence: His housing programme targets multiple-property concessions rather than removing every owner’s property; broad land redistribution remains an analogy.

axes.brief: His civil-rights and equal-citizenship programme rests on civil institutions rather than religious approval.
axes.counterEvidence: No public personal identity is established; retained holidays and charitable activity must be separated from clerical control of law.

axes.brief: He supports marriage equality, cannabis reform, sexual and gender equality and Indigenous constitutional change.
axes.counterEvidence: Progressive reform does not mean compulsory abandonment of every inherited custom; individual acceptance and institutional reform remain distinct.

axes.brief: He promotes clean-energy innovation and necessary housing while prioritising ecological limits and precaution over fossil-fuel expansion.
axes.counterEvidence: Backing lithium mining and public housing qualifies an absolute ban on habitat loss; medical enhancement positions are less directly documented.

axes.brief: He combines Indigenous self-government and local participation with national welfare, climate and housing coordination.
axes.counterEvidence: A federal rent-freeze fund works through state cooperation; nationwide policy goals are not evidence for abolishing state constitutions or local governments.

axes.brief: His explanations of inequality emphasise institutions, discrimination, social opportunities and learned political identity.
axes.counterEvidence: The evidence does not measure the causal weights of every psychological trait, so specific inherited-versus-learned choices remain educated contextual assumptions.

sources.title: Adam Bandt — biography and political views

religion.reason: The biographical material reviewed does not establish a public adult religious identity. Absence of an explicit declaration is not treated as no religion.
